title: Etale restriction and geometric-stalk recognition of prelog presentations
statement:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth]. On its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], let $M$ be a presheaf of commutative monoids (a contravariant functor with monoid-homomorphism restrictions) and $\gamma:M\to(\mathcal O_X,\cdot)$ a natural monoid homomorphism. For each etale $V\to X$, put $B_V=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, $E_V=\gamma_V^{-1}(B_V^\times)$, and let $P(V)$ be the commutative-monoid quotient of $M(V)\times B_V^\times$ by the congruence generated by $(me,u)\sim(m,\gamma_V(e)u)$ for $e\in E_V$.

Let $L$ be a log structure [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] and $\eta:P\to L$ a commutative-monoid sheafification [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification] satisfying $\alpha_L\eta_V([m,u])=\gamma_V(m)u$.

(1) For any etale $U\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], $U$ is locally Noetherian. Composition identifies its small etale site with the slice $X_{\mathrm{Et}}/U$, with the same covering families. Under this identification let $M_U$ be the restriction of $M$ and $P_U$ its quotient-of-pairs presheaf formed using $\gamma|_U$. Then $P_U(V\to U)=P(V\to X)$ with identical restrictions and relations. If $\eta_U:P_U\to L_U=P_U^\#$ is commutative-monoid sheafification, there is a unique canonical monoid-sheaf isomorphism $e:L_U\to L|_U$ satisfying $e\eta_U=\eta|_U$. It commutes with the structural maps to $\mathcal O_U$ and with the maps from $M_U$ and $\mathcal O_U^\times$.

(2) Let $K$ be another log structure, $v:M\to K$ a natural monoid homomorphism with $\alpha_Kv=\gamma$, and let $f:L\to K$ satisfy $\alpha_K f=\alpha_L$ and $f\eta_V([m,u])=v_V(m)j_{K,V}(u)$, where $j_K$ is the inverse units map. At a geometric point $\bar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point], take the stalk monoids and ring $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], let $\gamma_{\bar x}:M_{\bar x}\to A$ be induced, and put $E_{\bar x}=\gamma_{\bar x}^{-1}(A^\times)$ and $Q_{\bar x}=M_{\bar x}\oplus_{E_{\bar x}}A^\times$, with the same quotient relations. Suppose for every $\bar x$ that both maps
$$Q_{\bar x}\to L_{\bar x},\quad[m,a]\mapsto i_{\bar x}(m)j_{\bar x}(a),\qquad Q_{\bar x}\to K_{\bar x},\quad[m,a]\mapsto v_{\bar x}(m)j_{K,\bar x}(a)$$
are isomorphisms, where $i_V(m)=\eta_V([m,1])$ and $j_V(u)=\eta_V([1,u])$. Then $f$ is an isomorphism of log structures. In particular, if composition with $i$ has the universal mapping bijection for compatible maps from $M$ to every log structure $N$, composition with $v$ has that same bijection with $K$ in place of $L$.

proof.text: An etale map is locally of finite presentation. Its affine presentations have the form $R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_r)$, hence are finitely generated $R$-algebras. These pointwise affine data are exactly the criterion of lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion, so $U\to X$ is locally of finite type in the sense of def-weil-finite-type-morphism, and pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft gives local Noetherianity of $U$. Apply lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open to identify $U_{\mathrm{Et}}$ with $X_{\mathrm{Et}}/U$, by composition, with precisely the same covers. On an object $V\to U$ the restricted structure sheaf is $B_V=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$; its arrow maps are pullback of functions on $V$, independent of whether the structural map ends in $U$ or $X$.

For each $V\to U$, both constructions use the very same set $M(V)$, the same map $\gamma_V$, the same ring $B_V$ and therefore the same subset $E_V$. Their generating pairs $(me,u)\sim(m,\gamma_V(e)u)$ coincide. The generated congruences and quotient monoids consequently coincide. For an arrow $h:W\to V$ both restrictions send $[m,u]$ to $[M(h)(m),h^\sharp(u)]$. Naturality of $\gamma$ sends every generating relation to a generating relation on $W$, so these are identical presheaves, including their maps $m\mapsto[m,1]$, $u\mapsto[1,u]$ and $[m,u]\mapsto\gamma_V(m)u$.

source.place: VI 1.1, printed p.69, etale convention; agent-written verification of quotient presentations under the slice identification.

proof.text: By lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification, the underlying set maps of $\eta$ and $\eta_U$ are set sheafifications. Apply the SET-valued case of lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification to the underlying set presheaf of $P$ and the object $U$: $|L||_U$ is a sheafification of $|P|_U=|P_U|$, with unit $|\eta||_U$. Hence the unique set comparison from $|L_U|$ to $|L||_U$ preserving these units is bijective. The restriction $L|_U$ is a monoid sheaf: every matching family and its unique glue are computed over exactly the same covering family in $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$. The monoid universal property of $\eta_U$ now gives a unique monoid-sheaf map $e:L_U\to L|_U$ extending $\eta|_U$. Its underlying set map equals the preceding comparison by uniqueness for set sheafification. Thus $e$ is sectionwise bijective. Its inverses preserve multiplication and identity by applying $e$ to each required equation; naturality follows by applying $e$ to the restriction equation. They give the required canonical monoid-sheaf isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 00XZ (section-localize) and 00YR (section-sheaves-algebraic-structures), underlying set sheafification and monoid universal property.

proof.text: The map $P_U\to(\mathcal O_U,\cdot)$ given by $[m,u]\mapsto\gamma_V(m)u$ is a monoid map, since the two sides of each relation have the same image. Monoid sheafification extends it uniquely to the structural map $\alpha_{L_U}$. The maps $\alpha_{L_U}$ and $(\alpha_L|_U)e$ agree after $\eta_U$ by the formula in the hypothesis, so the uniqueness part of sheafification makes them equal. The identities with the maps from $M_U$ and $\mathcal O_U^\times$ follow by substituting $[m,1]$ and $[1,u]$ into $e\eta_U=\eta|_U$. In particular the structural comparison identifies the inverse image of units in $L_U$ with that in $L|_U$. The latter maps isomorphically to $\mathcal O_U^\times$ by the log axiom sectionwise, so $L_U$ is a log structure and $e$ is compatible with its log structure.

source.place: Tag 00YR (section-sheaves-algebraic-structures), uniqueness of extension; ILO VI 1.1, log convention.

proof.text: Set i(m)=eta([m,1]). The pair formula at (1,1), and preservation of identity by all monoid maps, give j_K(1)=1 even before invoking a sectionwise log-unit theorem. Its specialization at (m,1) then gives f i=v as natural transformations. Functoriality of the actual pointed-neighbourhood monoid colimit gives f_x i_x=v_x. Applying the colimit hom-ext principle to the structural maps gives alpha_K,x f_x=alpha_L,x. The maps on unit groups induced by both structural maps are bijections by the log axioms. Applying the injective one for K to the two candidate images of each ring unit proves f_x j_L,x=j_K,x. Thus the two pair maps from M_x times A^units commute with f_x directly, without choosing representatives of either input. Their kernels are equal: the structural chart maps agree, so their displayed generated congruences agree. Both pair maps are surjective by the two IsStalkChart hypotheses. For injectivity of f_x, lift two elements through the L pair map and use equality of the two kernels; for surjectivity, lift an element through the K pair map and apply the commuting equation. Hence f_x is bijective, equivalently an isomorphism of commutative monoids.

source.place: VI 1.1, printed p.69; agent-written elementary use of the given stalk-chart surjections and their exact kernel congruences, avoiding the representative argument.

proof.text: Choose algebraic closures of all residue fields, whose geometric points cover X. The forgetful functor from commutative monoids to sets preserves the pointed-neighbourhood colimits: pass to the u-small filtered final model and use its filtered-colimit preservation, then descend preservation along the final functor. The naturality of preservesColimitNatIso identifies the set stalk map with the conjugate of the forgotten monoid stalk map. It is therefore invertible at every chosen point. Apply lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks, implemented by isConservative_pointSmallEtale, to the underlying set sheaf map. Since the forgetful functor and its induced sheaf functor reflect isomorphisms, f itself is invertible. Composing alpha_K f=alpha_L with f inverse gives alpha_L f inverse=alpha_K.

source.place: Tag 03PU (theorem-exactness-stalks); algebraic closures and elementary inverses of bijective monoid maps.

proof.text: For every log structure N, define an equivalence between compatible maps K to N and compatible maps L to N by precomposition with f, inverse to precomposition with f inverse. The structural compatibility equations make both maps well defined, and the isomorphism identities give their inverse laws. The equation f i=v makes composition with i after this equivalence equal composition with v. Transfer injectivity using the equivalence and the assumed injectivity for i. For the compatible range, one inclusion is the structural equation v alpha_K=gamma; for the converse, obtain the unique compatible map L to N from the assumed range equality for i, and precompose with f inverse to obtain the required map K to N.

lean.statement: theorem etaleLogPresentation_comparison (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (M : X.Etaleᵒᵖ ⥤ CommMonCat.{u}) (γ : M ⟶ X.etaleStructurePresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat) (L : EtaleLogStructure X) (η : prelogPresentation γ ⟶ L.monoidSheaf.obj) (hη : IsPrelogPresentationSheafification γ L.monoidSheaf η) (hα : ∀ (W : X.Etale) (m : M.obj (op W)) (a : Γ(W.left, ⊤)ˣ), L.alpha.app (op W) (η.app (op W) (prelogPresentationPair γ W (m, a))) = @id Γ(W.left, ⊤) (γ.app (op W) m) * a.val) (K : EtaleLogStructure X) (v : M ⟶ K.monoidSheaf.obj) (hv : v ≫ K.alpha = γ) (f : L.monoidSheaf ⟶ K.monoidSheaf) (hf : f.hom ≫ K.alpha = L.alpha) (hpair : ∀ (W : X.Etale) (m : M.obj (op W)) (a : Γ(W.left, ⊤)ˣ), f.hom.app (op W) (η.app (op W) (prelogPresentationPair γ W (m, a))) = v.app (op W) m * prelogSectionUnit K W a) (hstalk : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X), L.IsStalkChart t (prelogStalkMap L.monoidSheaf (prelogPresentationIota γ L.monoidSheaf η) t).hom ∧ K.IsStalkChart t (prelogStalkMap K.monoidSheaf v t).hom) : (∃ e : L.monoidSheaf ≅ K.monoidSheaf, e.hom = f ∧ e.inv.hom ≫ L.alpha = K.alpha) ∧ (HasPrelogUniversalMapping γ L (prelogPresentationIota γ L.monoidSheaf η) → HasPrelogUniversalMapping γ K v)
